Done. IntegrationPolicy on HrfDescriptor, dispatched like DerivativePolicy/PenaltyPolicy; Primitive.definiteIntegral computes the box response as H(l) - H(l-d).

Closed forms: gamma (regularized lower incomplete gamma), Gaussian (normal CDF; erf via P(1/2, x^2) so one series serves both), SPMG1 (A1*gamma_inc(P1+1,x) - C*gamma_inc(P2+1,x)), SPMG temporal/dispersion derivatives (their primitives are the canonical kernel and the temporal derivative respectively — spmg1Deriv and spmg1SecondDeriv really are successive derivatives), SPMG2/3 stacked from components, boxcar analytic, and FIR/tent/B-spline as piecewise polynomials integrated with Gauss-Legendre of order ceil((p+1)/2) per piece (exact). Everything else keeps the trapezoid.

HrfDescriptor.derived CLEARS the policy, so a lagged/blocked/normalized kernel cannot inherit a primitive for a shape it no longer has — tested directly.

Key design point: the R parity anchor is preserved, not traded away. Integration is an explicit Exact | Trapezoid choice. Exact is the default; Trapezoid reproduces R's .block_offsets_weights and the duration corpus is still asserted against it bit-for-bit at 1e-9 across all four precisions. A new test asserts the complementary fact, that R's 6.06364 -> 6.12922 -> 6.15001 sequence is converging on the closed form (exact block peak 6.15088).

block() with infinite halfLife now routes through the same primitive; finite halfLife stays on quadrature because the integrand is not a box response.

New PrimitiveSuite (11 tests) validates every closed form against refined quadrature, against analytic overlap formulas for FIR/boxcar, and the incomplete gamma against the Erlang closed form. Verified JVM+JS: hrf 191, hrf-laws 77, design 146.
